dg-APL-211170.title: Continuum Aquatics Short AquaBlade Plastic Scraper for Glass Tanks
dg-APL-211170.summary: Continuum AquaBlade short hand scraper sized for nano and pico tanks; this glass version takes a metal blade.

dg-aquablade-m-steel-blades.title: AquaBlade-M Stainless Steel Replacement Blades
dg-aquablade-m-steel-blades.summary: Replacement metal blades for the AquaBlade glass scraper. Made of 316 stainless steel, so they're strong and resist rust, and they make quick work of stubborn coralline algae on glass.
rows: AquaBlade Short and Long scrapers (current and older models; the line is backward compatible)
warn: For acrylic tanks, use the acrylic-safe plastic (cyan) blade instead; only the plastic blade is sold as acrylic-safe.

dg-aquablade-p-acrylic-blades.title: AquaBlade-P Acrylic-Safe Replacement Blades (2 pack)
dg-aquablade-p-acrylic-blades.summary: Replacement cyan plastic blades for the AquaBlade scraper. They're made from a self-lubricating plastic that is softer than acrylic, so they clean acrylic tanks without scratching the panel itself.
rows: AquaBlade Short and Long scrapers (current and older models; the line is backward compatible)
warn: Because the blade is soft, it can pick up sand or gravel if it's pushed into the substrate, and grit will scratch acrylic. Check the edge often by running a fingertip or thumbnail across it.
Some low-grade acrylic is very soft. Test the blade on a hidden spot first.
